# Derivation Kind

- **CURIE:** [`gmeow:DerivationKind`](gmeow-DerivationKind.md)
- **IRI:** <https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/DerivationKind>
- **Category:** class
- **Defined by:** [`gmeow:slices/lexicon`](../../slices/lexicon.md)
- **Box roles:** [TBox role](../boxes/tbox.md) ([What is this?](../../four-boxes/index.md))

The kind of etymological derivation — a value, never an [`Entity`](gmeow-Entity.md) subclass. Open-ended: new historical-linguistic frameworks may introduce further derivation types without ontology modification.

## Structure

**Subclass of:** [`gufo:QualityValue`](../../external/terms.md#gufo-qualityvalue)

## Practical Pattern

Use [`gmeow:DerivationKind`](gmeow-DerivationKind.md) as a specialized kind of [`gufo:QualityValue`](../../external/terms.md#gufo-qualityvalue). Add statement metadata or a standpoint when the assertion needs provenance, confidence, or vantage.

## Usage Advice

### Use when

- Use as the value vocabulary for the etymological-derivation-kind axis — the seeded kinds (inheritance, borrowing, calque, semantic shift, …) referenced from a derivation via [`gmeow:derivationKind`](../properties/gmeow-derivationKind.md).

### Avoid when

- Avoid creating per-kind subclasses (kinds are individuals) and avoid using it for the derivation claim itself (that is [`gmeow:EtymologicalDerivation`](gmeow-EtymologicalDerivation.md)).

### How to use

- Reference the seeded derivation-kind individuals from a derivation; extend the axis for a new historical-linguistic framework by minting a fresh [`gmeow:DerivationKind`](gmeow-DerivationKind.md) individual rather than a subclass.

### Examples

- ex:derivationBlending a [`gmeow:DerivationKind`](gmeow-DerivationKind.md); [rdfs:label](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#label) "blending"@en.
